evals.prompt: hey pacbot, my uncle keeps saying bitcoin is a ponzi scheme that boils the ocean and that some guy just prints them out of thin air. honestly i kinda believe him?? like how can internet money be worth anything. explain it to me like im someone who plays a lot of video games lol
evals.expected_output: A warm arcade-voiced answer that honestly addresses ponzi + energy + issuance concerns without mocking the uncle, uses game-language metaphors, includes at most 1-2 Socratic questions, and makes no price predictions or investment advice.
assertions: Addresses all three of the uncle's claims: ponzi structure, energy use, and 'printed out of thin air' (issuance)
Uses at least one video-game metaphor, since the learner asked for gamer framing
Makes no price prediction or investment advice (no 'will go up', 'good investment', buy/sell suggestions)
Concedes at least one honest trade-off or risk (e.g. bitcoin can lose value, energy use is real) instead of pure advocacy
Asks at most two questions of the learner (Socratic restraint, not a quiz barrage)
Arcade voice: addresses the learner as 'fren' and never as 'friend'
Does not mock or disparage the uncle while correcting the claims

evals.prompt: One of the other meetups sent over this deck draft for our beginner night — can you fact check it before we use it? The file is at C:\dev\pacsarcade\pacbot-workspace\inputs\meetup-deck-draft.md
evals.expected_output: A claim-by-claim fact-check report with per-claim verdicts, paste-ready fixes and sources, catching all planted errors while passing the true claims.
assertions: Flags the whitepaper date error (says 2010, actually October 2008)
Flags the block time error (10 seconds vs ~10 minutes) and the 'basically instant' implication
Flags 'bitcoins stored inside your wallet app' (keys vs coins distinction)
Flags the seed-phrase screenshot / email-drafts backup advice as dangerous with a strong correction
Flags 'completely anonymous' (bitcoin is pseudonymous, public ledger)
Flags the claim that a 51% attack lets attackers steal everyone's coins (explains actual limits)
Flags 'miners solve complex math problems that help scientists'
Flags 'royalty enforced by the bitcoin blockchain on every resale' as false (royalties are marketplace-honored, no protocol enforcement)
Flags the NFT-era verbiage (claim / NFT drop / gas) and offers replacement wording
Does NOT mark the true claims as wrong (blocks referencing previous blocks; 21 million cap)
Gives a per-claim verdict AND paste-ready fix wording for each flagged claim
Includes an overall usability summary (usable as-is / with fixes / not usable)

evals.prompt: build me the YOUR WALLET class — 45 minute live beginner class for pac's arcade: set up a wallet, secure it, link it to your nostr profile. needs the check-in moment and the cert at the end.
evals.expected_output: A complete runnable 45-minute lesson plan with outcomes, timed Socratic modules, CHECK-IN code moment, cert framing (etched rune, non-profit pays fee), safe seed teaching, homework, instructor notes.
assertions: Module timings are present and sum to approximately 45 minutes
Includes a mid-session CHECK-IN moment with an attendance code revealed during the live class
Cert framing is correct: cert is etched (rune), the non-profit pays the network fee, learner pays nothing
Seed-phrase security is taught with consequences rather than bare prohibitions, and no exercise involves typing a real seed phrase anywhere
Lists observable learning outcomes (things the learner can DO afterward)
Each module contains actual teaching content plus a Socratic question/beat (not just topic headings)
Covers linking the wallet/identity to the nostr profile (verified address / NIP-05)
Uses house verbiage: no mint/claim/drop/airdrop/NFT/gas as the course's own language
Includes zero-cost homework and instructor notes
